text:
Tristan Luneau played one NHL game last season. This season he's playing 20 minutes a night on Anaheim's blue line, and The Athletic just named him among eight rising players under 23. The 2022 second-round pick has 4 goals and 14 points in 23 games.

What stands out is how much better the Ducks are with him out there. They get about 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, and more than 13 points better than when he sits, one of the biggest gaps on the team. His goals (4 on 1.8 expected) are running ahead of his chances, so the scoring is a little flattering. The play driving is the real headline.

He has the tools for it. His top skating speed ranks at the very top of the league and his shot is in the top 10% by speed. In junior he put up 83 points in his last QMJHL season, so the offense was always in there. Anaheim has leaned on him hard lately, including a 25-minute night against Colorado. We'd watch how he handles the tough matchups that come with those minutes.
